lede: Resolution grows from 4×4 to 32×32, and the last grid is one gray field.
title: Progressive GAN on CIFAR-10
question: Does growing the resolution from 4×4 to 32×32 keep CIFAR-10 samples stable?
process: The generator and discriminator losses are the same pair as in the vanilla GAN. What changes is the resolution. Training starts with a stable block at 4×4, then a fade and a stable block at 8×8, 16×16, and 32×32. During a fade, the new block is mixed in with a weight that moves from 0 to 1:

A new sample blends the previous resolution with the new one by α. The discriminator uses the inverse blend. The CIFAR-10 run uses 200 images per class and two epochs in each phase, 14 epochs in all. Epoch 6 is the last 8×8 batch that still looks varied. The scored 32×32 grid is one gray field, with sample standard deviation 0.104 against 0.493 on real images.

charts.title: Logged sample standard deviation as resolution grows

marks.summary: Epoch 1 is a stable 4×4 phase, with blend weight 1. The logged sample standard deviation is 0.581. The held-out discriminator loss is 1.458 and the generator loss is 0.774. The frames are large blocks of color, and they are not copies of one another.
Epoch 2 stays at 4×4. The logged sample standard deviation is 0.612, the high point of the run. The held-out discriminator loss is 1.403 and the generator loss is 0.857.

marks.summary: Epoch 5 is the first stable 8×8 epoch. The logged sample standard deviation bounces back to 0.504. The held-out discriminator loss is 0.945 and the generator loss is 1.092. The grid is still colorful and varied.

Epoch 6 is marked because it is the last stable 8×8 epoch where the fixed-noise batch still looks like different fields of color. The logged sample standard deviation is 0.414. The held-out discriminator loss is 0.734 and the generator loss is 1.786. Later growth makes the batch more alike. Epoch 14 is the scored 32×32 checkpoint, and that grid is one gray field.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: Epoch 13 is the first stable 32×32 epoch. The logged sample standard deviation drops to 0.131. The held-out discriminator loss is 0.634 and the generator loss is 1.403. The frames are pale and nearly the same.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: Epoch 14 is a stable 32×32 phase. The logged sample standard deviation is 0.104. The scored grid has sample standard deviation 0.1040 against 0.493 on real images, a ratio of 0.211. The collapse flag stays off because the cutoff is 0.20. The picture is one gray-purple field, repeated across the batch. On the log, the held-out discriminator loss is 1.520 and the generator loss is 0.700. Two epochs at 32×32 were enough for the samples to agree with one another, and not enough to grow an object.
marks.hover: Epoch 14, stable 32×32, scored ratio 0.211, collapse flag off.

reflection.worked: Epoch 6, the last stable 8×8 phase, still shows different fields of color. Early discriminator and generator losses stay near 1.
reflection.unexpected: By the scored 32×32 grid, every cell is one gray field, with sample standard deviation 0.104 against 0.493 on real images. The collapse flag stays off because the ratio is 0.211, just above 0.2.
reflection.why: Each new resolution gets two epochs on 2,000 images, and one of those epochs is a fade that is only half blended. A reasonable reading is that this is long enough to find one average color and too short to fit airplanes and trucks.
reflection.improve: Give the stable 16×16 and 32×32 phases more epochs before judging CIFAR-10, and plot the spread ratio against the 0.2 line so a batch of identical gray squares cannot sit just outside the flag.
